newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian industrial exports fall in first half.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian industrial exports fall in first half.

text.p: Bulgaria, hit by an economic crisis and mulling the introduction of a currency board to stabilise its finances, on Wednesday reported a drop in industrial exports this year.
"There is a drop in industrial exports in the first half of this year against the same period last year and its volume is $1 billion," Industry Minister Lyubomir Dachev told a news conference.
The decline is mainly related to the financial crisis and the lack of operating capital of industrial firms, he said.
The Varna shipyard, which has orders for building ships until 1998, is urgently seeking some $8 million to fully complete construction of new ships, deputy industry minister Svetoslav Dimitrov said.

He said foreign firms had made payments to the shipyard through banks in Europe which refuse to transfer the money to the Varna shipyard because of a lack of confidence in the Bulgarian banking system.
Last year, industrial products exports rose 24.5 percent to $3.9 billion over 1994, 75.5 percent of total exports.
The petrol and chemical industry has the largest share in exports with some 35 percent of the total.
Exports of machine building, electronics and electrical engineering were 30 percent of the total, ferrous and non-ferrous metalurgy 20 percent, and light industry products 13 percent.
One of the ministry's main targets is to restore its former markets such as Russia and the ex-Soviet republics, Deputy Industry Minister Svetoslav Dimitrov said.
He said Russia considered Bulgaria, unlike Romania, as a developed country and imposed high customs fees on its goods.
"We are seeking the establishment of joint ventures in order to overcome such a regime (of customs)," Dimitrov said.
The ministry is preparing a scheme for liberalising custom fees on imported industrial goods from countries with which Bulgaria has not signed an agreement for the establishment of free trade zones.
Bulgaria as a new member of the World Trade Organisation is due to reduce customs fees on some 200 items from December 1. Duties on other goods will be reduced in January, ministry officials said.

The Bulgarian lev reached record lows against the dollar on Wednesday. Introduction of a currency board proposed by the International Monetary Fund would stabilise the economy and could improve the climate for foreign trade.
